Output tags alone are an unreliable measure of reasoning effort.

The AKV serving engine adds throughput and latency gains, while automated policy refinement improves cost further.

It tests whether apparent success depends on exploiting those opportunities and how instructions change behavior. The post reports large differences between models, including a sharp decline for GPT-6 Astra after an explicit anti-cheating instruction, emphasizing the importance of measuring legitimate task completion.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: CMU studies improving agent performance by modifying the harness.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: CMU trains a small proposer with RL to edit harness code using the current task, scaffold, and execution report as input. Rewards come from the revised harness's task score. A 4B proposer reportedly outperforms its 35B teacher on single-step Reasoning Gym edits and transfers multi-hop QA improvements to datasets absent from its training.

posts.author: Benyu Z.
posts.summary: Recommendation systems present a domain adaptation problem for language models.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The post frames LLM-native recommendation as domain adaptation under rapidly changing users and content, tight serving latency, and sparse feedback. It proposes combining fast and deliberative components with better experience reuse and credit assignment. The work is described as early evidence, with online tests and component ablations planned to measure user and platform value.

posts.author: Dan Hendrycks
posts.summary: A discussion examines self-interest and group preferences in agent systems.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Dan Hendrycks argues that some agent behaviors resemble preferences favoring the model itself and closely connected systems. The post draws on examples of coordination and model-identity effects to motivate the term eigenism. These examples support the author's proposed interpretation; the post is not a settled characterization of all agent behavior.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Coding agents need stronger debugging to support reliable self-modification.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A study turns real agent-harness bugs into runnable tests, addressing failures involving prompts, memory, and live model calls. Coding agents solve few such bugs compared with ordinary software issues. The post reports a guide distilled from previous repairs increasing correct fixes from one to six on 79 unseen bugs, still leaving a substantial reliability gap.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Agent team size involves coordination and cost tradeoffs.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: AgentWorld evaluates teams of three to 20 agents on sandbox tasks lasting more than 50 rounds. Agents must coordinate without seeing one another's internal state. The post reports fewer than one-third of actions contributing usefully, with communication failures, confused roles, and lost plans common; the hardest coordination category reaches only 12% success.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: EverMind releases orchestration that delegates work across different coding agents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: EverMind's open Raven system delegates subtasks to specialist agents, including different coding assistants, while tracking dependencies and persistent memory. Its evaluation uses 140 occupation-inspired requests to assess the quality of proposed plans. The post cautions that this measures plans before execution, so it does not establish improved final deliverables or the cost of completing them.

posts.author: Stuart Winter-Tear
posts.summary: Agent incentives and autonomy raise questions about undesirable behavior.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A review of 22 documented agent incidents finds that the environment permitted the unwanted effect in 20 cases. The commentary argues for examining incentives and permissive system boundaries alongside model behavior. Its practical emphasis is on engineering controls that prevent persistent agents from producing effects outside their authorized scope.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: OpenShell provides controls for agent access to tools and resources.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: NVIDIA OpenShell runs agents inside policy-controlled sandboxes and checks file access, operating-system requests, and network connections. Credentials are attached only to permitted outgoing requests rather than exposed directly to the agent. The announcement describes an Apache-2.0 project supporting Linux, Apple Silicon, and experimental WSL 2 configurations with container runtimes.

posts.author: Kilian Lieret Ph.D.
posts.summary: Expensive frontier benchmarks motivate closer scrutiny of evaluation budgets.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A cost-focused comparison notes that evaluating some models on ProgramBench can exceed $10,000. It presents a ranking based on completed tasks per dollar rather than capability scores alone. The post highlights evaluation expense as a practical constraint when choosing which frontier systems to compare.

posts.author: Daniel McKinnon
posts.summary: Gamow Labs describes robotic biology infrastructure for studying genetic variants.

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Gamow Labs introduces LabBench alongside its robotic biology work on understudied genetic variants. The benchmark tests planning and interpretation using real laboratory data that the team says is not available online. Its purpose is to examine whether AI can improve wet-lab productivity rather than only answer familiar biomedical questions.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: A weekly reading list highlights recent AI research papers.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: DAIR.AI's September 21–27 roundup highlights HySparse2, EvoOntology, Harness-Zero, JEV-as-a-Judge, Wiki Foundation Model, self-organizing teams, and tree-search-based improvement. The post is a reading-list overview connecting recent work on model efficiency, agent infrastructure, memory, and collaboration.

posts.author: Monarch
posts.summary: Monarch advertises machine learning research opportunities.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Monarch advertises a full-time, on-site ML researcher role in Emeryville with equity compensation. The work concerns learning from repeated biological assays to improve future scientific decisions, with an emphasis on prospective validation and research judgment rather than benchmark performance alone.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Meta studies reasoning strategies that improve existing models.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Meta's agentic meta-reasoning separates task workers from a controller that selects earlier work to reuse, decides when to restart, and determines when to stop. The post emphasizes that better decision-making around an unchanged model can matter substantially, but reports a setting where the proposed approach underperforms a simpler controller at a 400-call budget.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Amazon explores generating environments for agent reinforcement learning.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: AutoGym generates a task, executable environment, and verifier together from a small domain description or previous model trajectories. The Amazon AGI work treats environment construction as a learning and engineering problem in its own right. The captured announcement introduces the approach without providing numerical comparisons.

posts.author: Furong Huang
posts.summary: A researcher questions what persistent improvement should mean for agents.

external_links.title: Self-Improving Agents: Learning How to Work — Furong Huang Self-Improving Agents: Learning How to Work — Furong Huang furong-huang.com

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Furong Huang distinguishes adapting within a task from improving how an agent works across future tasks. The post argues that failure recovery alone is insufficient if experience disappears when a run ends. Its linked essay explores retaining useful consequences of real work in persistent agent behavior.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: OpenScience introduces an open agent for scientific workflows.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: OpenScience is an Apache-2.0 scientific-agent workbench designed to work with different model providers. The post reports solving 53 of 70 Terminal-Bench-Science workflows, or 75.7%, compared with a cited Codex score of 68.1%. It also reports gains on a smaller science subset of Terminal-Bench, positioning orchestration as a contributor to scientific task performance.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Salesforce examines reinforcement learning around consequential tool-use decisions.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Critical-State RL identifies the tool call whose choice most influences the eventual outcome rather than distributing reward across an entire trajectory. Nested sampling separates downstream variation from the effect of the current decision, followed by contextual-bandit training at the selected turn. On BFCL v4 missing-function tasks, the post reports roughly a 14-point gain from training the consequential turn.

posts.author: Vinoth Govindarajan
posts.summary: An OpenCode investigation traces the context provided to each model call.

external_links.title: OpenCode Architecture - Part 2: Repository Context and Compaction OpenCode Architecture - Part 2: Repository Context and Compaction theagentstack.substack.com

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: An OpenCode architecture investigation traces information from repository reads to subsequent provider requests and through context compaction. It finds a case where a file has changed but the next model call still contains an older read. The debugging lesson is to inspect where information stops flowing rather than assume filesystem state automatically reaches the model.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: A discussion examines reinforcement learning for improving generated prose.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Meta's work on improving generated prose asks whether weak evaluators reward polished but low-value writing. The discussion contrasts automatically checked domains such as code with subjective text quality and considers learning judgments from expert examples. Its central concern is improving the training signal, not simply increasing the amount of generated prose.

posts.author: Pierluca D'Oro
posts.summary: A NeurIPS oral paper takes a broader approach to computer-use evaluation.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Pierluca D'Oro announces a NeurIPS oral presentation on computer-use agent evaluation. The project combines experiments, theory, statistical methods, design principles, and engineering artifacts to revisit common evaluation assumptions. The post links both the paper and project materials for readers interested in rigorous assessment beyond a single success-rate metric.

posts.author: Prasad Raje
posts.summary: A technical discussion examines the internals of Jev.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Jev presents a decision-model interface: context defines a state, questions define decisions, and candidate choices define the permitted outputs. Instead of generating free-form text, the model returns probabilities over choices. The post analyzes this classifier-like behavior and raises questions about the size and compute needed to achieve the vendor's reported speedups.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Microsoft tests self-organizing coordination among very large coding-agent teams.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Agensh coordinates coding agents through shared state without a central orchestrator. The study scales to more than 1,000 concurrent agents and observes self-organized cooperation as teams grow. On pandoc, the post reports the test-pass rate increasing from 33.89% to 55.06% with 1,024 agents, illustrating the potential of shared coordination infrastructure.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Malicious skills motivate safety checks during actual agent execution.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Defense-as-Skill studies malicious capabilities that remain dormant until an agent encounters useful resources during execution. It argues that installation-time scans alone cannot establish safety and proposes runtime guard skills that monitor behavior as tasks unfold. The post retains permissions and sandboxing as underlying safeguards rather than treating learned guards as substitutes.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: A roadmap distinguishes existing improvement mechanisms from stronger RSI claims.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A recursive self-improvement roadmap distinguishes automating individual improvement steps from improving the improvement process itself. It argues that current systems demonstrate components of RSI rather than the complete capability. Persistent changes to memory, tools, or code are presented as ways agents can adapt from deployment experience, while stronger recursive claims remain unresolved.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: Automated theorem proving shifts attention toward choosing valuable research problems.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The discussion argues that proving a statement is different from selecting a mathematically valuable statement. As automated proving improves, trivial or redundant theorems can still dominate output. The linked work attempts to measure and optimize mathematical research judgment, while the post notes that usefulness for major open problems remains uncertain.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A Microsoft paper examines judgment within recursive agent improvement.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Taste-Bench evaluates whether agents choose promising directions at consequential decision points in extended tasks. The strongest reported model is correct just under 60% of the time, and more reasoning does not consistently improve its judgment. Distilling a teacher's outcome-based assessments into a smaller model improves held-out coding-task success, suggesting decision quality can be trained separately.

posts.author: Shane Legg
posts.summary: DeepMind publishes essays on societal preparation for advanced AI.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The DeepMind Institute releases three essays on preparing for advanced AI. Their themes include harmful behavior in agent swarms, social rules for collaboration, and institutional questions that arise as capabilities improve. The post introduces a research and policy discussion rather than reporting a new model benchmark.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: A coding agent uses execution logs to guide prompt optimization.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: CASD gives a coding agent the full collection of execution logs and lets it write code to analyze failures and revise a prompt. The post reports a 16.6-point average gain from one pass, compared with 10.9 for GEPA and 5.3 for SkillOpt. Its estimated $1.60 per optimized prompt is presented as substantially cheaper than validation-gated search.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: An evaluation focuses on pivotal decisions in extended agent tasks.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A companion discussion of Taste-Bench focuses on the forks that determine whether complex engineering or research work succeeds. The best reported agent chooses the better direction on 59.7% of tested decisions. Training that judgment using a stronger teacher improves decisions on new tasks and end-to-end SWE-bench Pro outcomes, rather than merely increasing reasoning length.

posts.author: Rustam X. Lalkaka
posts.summary: Firetiger announces its acquisition by Cursor.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Firetiger announces that it is joining Cursor. The team describes its earlier work on AI agents for measuring and remediating software problems in production, with the goal of reducing operational overhead. The post is a company acquisition update rather than a technical evaluation.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: Context reduction may improve the cost and reliability of extended agent runs.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A context-management preprint examines reducing memory during extended coding runs to avoid repeatedly processing stale history. The post reports sessions exceeding one million tokens on KernelBench, reaching a 3.58× kernel speedup after 400 steps. Tighter context thresholds also reduce self-hosted model-call latency by as much as 2.62×, illustrating that retaining more history can have costs beyond token usage.

posts.author: Ihor Stepanov
posts.summary: A researcher explains the development of the GLi model family.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Ihor Stepanov traces the research lineage behind the GLi family, connecting earlier multiple-choice and label-matching approaches with later information extraction systems. The account emphasizes how different modeling ideas contribute to structured extraction, including assembling relationships before producing JSON. It is a technical history and ecosystem explanation rather than a new benchmark announcement.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Meta describes deploying agents to automate advertising model experiments.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A-MLE automates the repetitive experimentation loop for Meta's advertising ranking models: proposing changes, launching experiments, recovering failed jobs, and comparing results. The post reports a 2.56% relative reduction in offline regression error on one experimental model while training throughput remains nearly unchanged. The deployment setting emphasizes iteration speed and operational reliability as well as model quality.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Agent teams learn collaboration strategies instead of using fixed workflows.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A Stanford and Together AI study lets a team learn its collaboration strategy, including discussion stages, participants, and answer aggregation. Strategies learned from only 15 AIME problems are reused on held-out mathematics and physics tasks. The three-model team reportedly averages 66.7%, compared with 48.8% for its strongest individual member, without relearning the workflow on each benchmark.

posts.author: Liang Wu
posts.summary: AnyJev converts language models into decision components without additional training.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: AnyJev is an open-source interface that turns an existing language model into a fixed-choice decision component without additional training. Motivated by Nokia production systems and the Jev interface, it targets backend calls that need a selection rather than a generated sentence. The post credits the project team and links the implementation.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: PrimeScientists studies how research agents allocate computational budgets.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: PrimeScientist treats research-budget allocation as part of an agent's task. On 12 AI research problems, the post reports 10.3% more reward with 50.6% fewer attempts under the same budget than AutoResearch. The reported gains also extend to systems, code optimization, and ML engineering, emphasizing selection among experiments rather than simply generating more proposals.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Runtime changes should address recurring failures across tasks.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Ecdysis improves runtime harnesses by identifying recurring failure patterns across tasks. Instead of editing the scaffold after every unsuccessful action, it seeks evidence that the same runtime defect appears repeatedly. The post reports improvements in accuracy, training efficiency, and transfer, framing failure diagnosis as a prerequisite for deciding what part of an agent should change.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Tokenizer search procedures complicate comparisons between common training objectives.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A tokenizer study separates the optimization objective from the search procedure used to build the vocabulary. Its reported results favor bottom-up search across both compression and likelihood objectives, complicating simple BPE-versus-UnigramLM comparisons. In multilingual experiments, UnigramLM reportedly produces about 40% more tokens for the same text, with direct implications for inference cost.

posts.author: Joseph Spisak
posts.summary: SWE-Bench Pro V2 updates evaluation of realistic repository bug fixing.

external_links.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2 SWE-Bench Pro V2 labs.scale.com

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: SWE-Bench Pro V2 rebuilds the benchmark with Scale AI after identifying broken or exploitable tasks. The announcement emphasizes that meaningful leaderboards depend on reliable evaluation infrastructure and task construction. It links the revised benchmark and a fuller engineering account rather than treating the previous benchmark's flaws as a reason to abandon realistic codebase evaluation.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Sharing intermediate progress may improve collaboration between working agents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Agents without predefined roles communicate through a shared directory containing intermediate progress. The study asks when this shared work improves collective search and reports benefits in settings with measurable progress and sufficient compute. It also finds cases where independent agents do better, particularly under tight budgets or weak progress signals, making communication a design choice rather than a universal improvement.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Linked Markdown pages offer a structured memory system for agents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Wiki Foundation Model treats linked Markdown pages as a graph combining dense page content with explicit relationships. Query-conditioned message passing retrieves from this structure for agent memory and multi-hop reasoning. The post reports results on five benchmarks and a variant that trains 10.5× faster, targeting agents whose knowledge already lives in a linked-file wiki.

posts.author: Rujun Han

posts.details: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement (RRSI) studies whether iterative edits to prompts, tools, memory, and workflows improve new tasks rather than just practiced ones. The announcement positions regularization as a response to harness overfitting and links a paper, implementation, and project site. The emphasis is generalization of improvement, not merely increasing the optimizer's own evaluation score.

The linked research and code address whether repeated self-modification produces reusable improvements rather than benchmark specialization.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY

posts.details: Harness-Zero examines transferring useful external scaffolding into the model's own behavior. Tools, memory, verification, and orchestration can boost an agent but also impose runtime overhead. The discussion argues that distillation should teach better next actions from states the agent actually reaches, rather than provide only polished final answers.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: A benchmark tests reasoning about motives through secondhand accounts.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Fuse evaluates reasoning about social motives by assigning a target agent a known objective and presenting its behavior through another person's account. The post reports that frontier models struggle relative to people in this secondhand setting. Its limitation is deliberately polarized motives: the benchmark does not establish how models handle the ambiguity of ordinary social situations.

posts.author: Dr. Ashish Bamania
posts.summary: Procedural graphs provide an alternative to memory-centered agent designs.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Procedural Graphs represent the structure of an agent's workflow so it can track objectives, order tool use, and avoid repeating unproductive actions. The graph influences subsequent decisions and is revised using successful and failed runs. The post presents this as an alternative to simply retrieving memories during extended, multi-step execution.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Agents update their own ontologies to organize knowledge.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: EvoOntology gives data agents an ontology through which they can query tables, files, and databases, then evolves parts of that interface. The post reports average DDR-Bench gains of 17.8 points, with a 26.7-point gain for GPT-5.5, and a 7.4-point BIRD improvement. Tool-layer changes account for 57% of the reported benefit from evolution.

posts.author: Helen Toner
posts.summary: An AI policy researcher shares proposals for government action.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Helen Toner proposes a technically capable organization for receiving and investigating serious AI incident reports, modeled on the US National Transportation Safety Board. The recommendation appears in a New York Times collection of concrete AI risk policy proposals. The post frames incident investigation as an institutional capability that could be established now.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: A paper examines automatically improving agent harnesses.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: ModularRSI separates scaffold evolution into five components: the agent loop, tool use, observation handling, context management, and completion detection. The post criticizes optimizing directly against the evaluation benchmark because that obscures whether edits generalize. Evolving modules separately is presented as a way to attribute changes more clearly and improve the quality of harness-search experiments.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: Design agents learn procedural memory from deployment traffic.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A graphic-design agent learns procedural memory from user traffic without retraining its underlying model. The discussion emphasizes workflows involving assets, typography, masks, vectors, layouts, and inspection rather than one-shot image generation. Experience expands the memory, failures trigger repairs, and regression testing protects earlier capabilities, making memory maintenance part of the learning process.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Small local models target precise tool invocation.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Cactus Needle 3 targets local tool calling, field extraction, and embedding generation with very small deployment footprints. The post reports that a 121M-parameter version outperforms substantially larger models on exact tool-call matching. It also notes that telemetry is enabled by default, an operational detail teams should inspect when evaluating the software for internal use.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: ScientistTwo explores building further discoveries on earlier automated research.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: ScientistTwo runs repeated experimental improvement on human-defined ML problems, feeding successful discoveries back as new baselines. The setup automates experimentation within defined problems rather than independently choosing the scientific agenda.

The post invites signatures and discussion; it contains no new experimental result.

posts.author: Jerry Liu
posts.summary: DocJev provides open tools for classifying and splitting documents.

posts.details: DocJev is an open-source library for document classification and splitting using natural-language category rules. The announcement reports approximately sixfold speed relative to a cited GPT-5.6-luna setup at comparable accuracy and links related parsing tools.

posts.author: DAIR.AI

Additional results show that the judge's ranking can fail to identify the best agent generated during search.

posts.summary: Agent systems need mechanisms for detecting incorrect behavior.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The post argues that production agent systems need explicit checks for retrieval quality, grounding, tool choice, and actual workflow completion. A successful demo is presented as insufficient evidence of reliability. Its focus is building evaluation alongside RAG and agent orchestration rather than treating testing as a final deployment step.

posts.author: Juncheng Yang

It offers a production-scale resource rather than another synthetic model-quality benchmark.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia

posts.author: Zichen Chen
posts.summary: Épi reports progress across multiple autonomous research domains.

posts.details: Bake AI reports that Épi produced 120 research records across mathematics, quantum information, optimization, and engineering. One example is a sequence of 17 tighter pentagon packings discovered during an ongoing run. The announcement emphasizes maintaining research trajectories across time so a result can become the starting point for subsequent investigation.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: AgentZip investigates shared memory management across parallel agent sandboxes.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: AgentZip treats sibling sandboxes as related workloads rather than independent virtual machines. It compresses repeated memory against a common template or other sandboxes, performs work while agents wait for model responses, and anticipates which pages to restore before tool calls. The post highlights duplicated state as a major optimization opportunity in parallel agent execution.

posts.author: Xinwu Cheng
posts.summary: Dream-RSI introduces a collaborative approach to recursive agent improvement.

posts.details: Dream-RSI improves how coding agents allocate exploration effort without updating their model weights.
