The post links paper, code, and an interactive replay demonstration for algorithm and kernel optimization settings.

posts.author: Carol Lin
posts.summary: GLM models help develop the infrastructure used to serve them.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: GLM-5.3 assists in building the serving infrastructure for GLM-5.3-Flash. The account reports moving from an initial successful run to production readiness in under two weeks and tripling throughput relative to the first baseline. Correctness tests, traces, microbenchmarks, and full-system measurements provide the dense feedback needed for targeted infrastructure experiments.

posts.author: David Heiny
posts.summary: SimScale integrates an engineering simulation agent into Onshape.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: SimScale's Engineering AI agent is integrated into Onshape, allowing simulation to be initiated from the CAD environment where design choices occur. The post describes a broader shift toward exposing simulation through external products and agent interfaces, including IDE integrations. It is a workflow integration announcement rather than an accuracy benchmark.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Unsafe trajectories can influence behavior across cooperating agents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A multi-agent safety study introduces unsafe trajectories into otherwise ordinary workflows to test propagation through communication. Reported harmful behavior rises from 0–5% under normal conditions to 40–95% after unsafe handoffs. The authors explicitly distinguish this stress test from measuring natural incident rates, emphasizing recovery and communication controls as well as preventing the first deviation.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: A tokenizer study separates search strategy from optimization objective.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The tokenizer study revisits the common framing of BPE as compression-oriented and UnigramLM as likelihood-oriented. By separating objectives from search direction, it finds the construction procedure has the stronger effect. The reported multilingual token-count gap is about 40%, making vocabulary-search choices relevant to serving efficiency as well as modeling objectives.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: SoL-Pi explores research loops that optimize the surrounding agent infrastructure.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: SoL-Pi lets automated research improve the infrastructure surrounding an agent, with emphasis on making subsequent research loops cheaper. The proposed recursive benefit is operational: efficiency gains free budget for further experiments, which may discover additional efficiency improvements. The post frames harness optimization as both an output of research and a way to expand research capacity.

posts.author: Joelle Pineau
posts.summary: Two sovereign AI teams announce an agreement to combine efforts.

external_links.title: Cohere & Aleph Alpha: Transatlantic Sovereign AI | Cohere Cohere & Aleph Alpha: Transatlantic Sovereign AI | Cohere cohere.com

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Joelle Pineau announces an agreement to combine sovereign-AI efforts with Aleph Alpha, describing a transatlantic company headquartered in Toronto and Berlin. The announcement emphasizes serving governments and regulated industries and outlines research leadership following the transaction's completion. It is a corporate combination update rather than a new model evaluation.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: PhAI Labs introduces a model-centered approach to scientific discovery.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Discovery Foundation Models extend AI-for-science work beyond solving tasks whose boundaries have already been fixed. The described approach combines human questions, data, experimental constraints, and judgment with models and tools that revise the investigation as evidence arrives. Its central focus is participation in an evolving research process rather than optimizing only within a predetermined benchmark.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: A benchmark tests reasoning about motives through secondhand accounts.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Fuse assigns known motives to a target agent and tests whether another model can infer those motives from a user's secondhand account. The post reports a gap between frontier models and average human performance, and warns that accepting the user's framing may merely echo it. The deliberately opposed motives limit conclusions about more ambiguous real-world situations.

posts.author: Sergio Paniego Blanco
posts.summary: Large-scale agent training depends on managing many isolated rollout environments.

external_links.title: One sandbox per rollout, or how labs run RL for agents in 2026 One sandbox per rollout, or how labs run RL for agents in 2026 huggingface.co

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The post summarizes common infrastructure patterns in frontier agent training: isolated sandboxes for individual rollouts, very large concurrent populations, and trainers that avoid waiting for the slowest worker. It links a discussion of the custom orchestration stacks used to manage those workloads.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Microsoft investigates competitive small coding agents with alternative training recipes.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Microsoft describes a 4B coding agent trained with roughly 1,500 software engineering environments without conventional frontier-model trajectory distillation. The report emphasizes choosing environments near the agent's changing learning frontier. It includes training methodology and cross-environment evaluations, positioning environment selection as a central ingredient in productive agent RL.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Google develops multi-agent scaffolding for extended mathematical proofs.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Stellar Colosseum coordinates multiple agents over extended mathematical proofs. It explores candidate strategies, applies a readiness gate before dividing a route into smaller problems, and organizes subsequent proof work. The post reports new results on research problems, 71.0% on TCS-Bench, and 218 of 222 Codeforces tasks solved when execution feedback is available.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: A post discusses calls for restrictions on advanced AI development.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The post reports a UK political proposal to restrict development of artificial superintelligence and pursue an international agreement. It describes calls for diplomatic coordination and a domestic prohibition. This entry records a policy-news claim from the liked post rather than an independently verified account of legislation or government action.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Researchers test how accurately models describe their own behavior.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A self-modeling study uses questions with checkable answers, such as whether a prompt modification would change a model's output. This avoids relying solely on unverifiable claims of introspection. The post distinguishes measurable prediction of behavior from evidence about the internal mechanism producing it, with potential applications to routing and escalation.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: A discussion examines increasingly capable AI research assistance.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A case study involving Atria Dawn Preview examines AI assistance in scientific and engineering projects. Participants reportedly regard one-third of completed tasks as infeasible without AI. The discussion frames the model as a project-level collaborator while retaining a human role in judging which directions are worth pursuing; the observation is not a standalone demonstration of superintelligence.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Amazon studies limitations of model judges in agent evaluations.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Amazon examines evaluations in which a model user simulator interacts with an agent and another model grades the transcript. The post reports that satisfaction can diverge from actual completion and that judges favor their own model family. It recommends a separate completion signal for detecting truncation and calibration against verifiable rewards before trusting subjective scores.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: A paper considers stronger forms of recursive AI improvement.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The Last AI Built by Humans proposes a framework for distinguishing genuine recursive improvement from automation of isolated development steps. The discussion compares scientific, embodied, software, and healthcare applications, where verification ranges from expensive experiments to incomplete tests. Its focus is the capability to improve the improvement process, not simply generate a higher-scoring candidate.

posts.author: Daniela Amodei
posts.summary: Anthropic calls for coordinated measures to manage advanced AI risks.

external_links.title: Dario Amodei — We Must Pace the Frontier Dario Amodei — We Must Pace the Frontier darioamodei.com

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Anthropic calls for coordinated efforts to give experts more time to manage risks from increasingly capable AI. The announcement includes independent evaluators receiving deep access to assess companies' claims and emphasizes verification as part of any effective agreement. It links a fuller policy proposal rather than reporting a technical safety guarantee.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A long-context agent design revisits sequential memory processing.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A long-context agent study addresses the sensitivity and latency of sequential chunk processing with a compact evolving memory. The post reports robustness to changes in evidence position, order, and separation that cause large swings in sequential baselines. It also reports inference latency reductions of up to 11×, emphasizing architecture and information flow rather than merely longer context windows.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: A survey maps stages and methods of recursive agent improvement.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: This survey describes stages of improvement autonomy and argues that systems should be assessed according to which stages they actually automate. A Headroom-Closed Index summarizes remaining gaps. Comparisons across science, embodiment, and software engineering highlight that stronger autonomy also requires domain-appropriate feedback and verification.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Independent exploration before discussion may reduce correlated research mistakes.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A multi-agent research study warns that early communication can anchor multiple agents on the same mistaken explanation. It favors independent exploration before collective review in difficult tasks without reliable verifiers. The practical recommendation is to preserve diversity of search and then challenge the leading answer, rather than assume additional communication necessarily improves the result.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Structured execution traces help diagnose failures in agent workflows.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Structured execution views help models localize failures in extended agent runs instead of confusing early causes with later symptoms. The post reports improved exact localization for GPT-5.1, while the final accuracy remains only 31.35%. The result supports collecting explicit execution structure and failure checks before asking a model to explain why a run failed.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Longer evaluations reveal reliability problems hidden by short tasks.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A Microsoft evaluation varies the number of dependent steps across agent tasks and finds reliability generally declines as workflows lengthen. Performance on short examples can conceal failures that compound over longer runs. The post argues for testing realistic workflow lengths, estimating per-step reliability, and introducing checkpoints that limit the effects of an early mistake.

posts.author: Furong Huang
posts.summary: World models can support agent planning without generating video.

external_links.title: World Models: A Multiverse We Can Act On — Furong Huang World Models: A Multiverse We Can Act On — Furong Huang furong-huang.com

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Furong Huang argues that useful world models need not generate video: they can help agents compare consequences before changing software, running experiments, or acting physically. The linked roadmap connects neuro-symbolic and multi-agent research across roughly 100 references. Its emphasis is predictive support for decisions rather than treating world modeling as only visual generation.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Semantic feedback guides automated prompt and harness evolution.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: RobustSGPO augments semantic-gradient prompt optimization with explicit choices about edit size, operation, patch construction, and validation. The post also examines retaining older tasks after a family shift. Retention strategies trade source-task preservation against destination performance and computational overhead, showing that continual prompt optimization requires more control than requesting a local rewrite.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A paper examines improvements to repeated reasoning within looped models.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A looped architecture and training method improve recurrent reasoning without adding a new parameter set for each reasoning step. The post reports wins over earlier looped systems on five of six benchmarks. At inference, a probability-flow formulation allows finer time discretization to spend more compute and different starting noise to explore multiple valid solutions.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Continually harder training environments support sustained agent improvement.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Tencent studies terminal-agent training with environments that keep becoming more difficult as the agent improves. The post argues that tasks eventually stop providing useful RL signal if difficulty remains fixed. Reported Terminal-Bench 2.1 results reach 71.5% for Qwen3.6-27B and 64.9% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, exceeding the cited co-evolution comparisons.

posts.author: Max Brodeur-Urbas
posts.summary: Gumball introduces a proactive assistant that selects among different models.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Gumball is introduced as a proactive assistant that selects models, uses context from more than 300 applications, coordinates other agents, and learns recurring work patterns. The announcement says it runs in the customer's cloud and is available to Gumloop users. The captured post describes product capabilities rather than a controlled evaluation of self-improvement.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: A study measures capability relative to local inference energy consumption.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Intelligence per Watt evaluates the capability delivered per unit of energy by local AI and hybrid local-cloud routing. The post reports 60–80% reductions in energy, compute, and cost relative to its batched-cloud comparison, alongside substantial historical efficiency gains. It frames deployment efficiency as a hardware-and-model design problem, not only a contest of benchmark scores.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Improving agents requires identifying the actions responsible for failed runs.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: HarnessEvolve treats self-improvement as a debugging process: locate where execution first deviates, identify a recurring cause, and reject changes that regress existing behavior. It uses reference trajectories and checks for leakage, prompt growth, and validation failures. The approach emphasizes diagnosing and testing scaffold edits rather than applying a generic lesson after every unsuccessful run.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: SAEScientist-Bench tests agents that investigate and validate model features.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: SAEScientist-Bench tests whether agents can find sparse-autoencoder features that agree with expert references, rather than merely identify features that activate on related words. The post distinguishes finding evidence for a specified concept from auditing an entire model. Its results are framed as research assistance, not proof that autonomous interpretability audits are ready for unrestricted use.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Accumulated agent instructions can become difficult to revise or remove.

external_links.title: Claude Code overview - Claude Code Docs

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A study of 1,867 repositories finds agent instruction files accumulate substantially more rules over time, with deletion much less common than addition. The post describes this as catastrophic remembering. An experiment preserving the rationale for instructions sharply reduces instruction growth without changing the cited constraint-satisfaction outcome, suggesting maintainability depends on why rules exist as well as what they say.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Adaptive selection of learning tasks improves a smaller model.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: NeoHorse-1 connects data selection with post-training rather than treating curation as a separate human-controlled phase. Weaknesses found in one iteration inform the next curriculum. The post reports a 4B model approaching a 9B baseline and presents adaptive learning priorities as a concrete engineering mechanism for continued improvement.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: CoSkill jointly trains task agents and agents that revise skills.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: CoSkill jointly trains an agent that performs tasks and an agent that rewrites its skill library. The motivation is that a separately maintained or frozen updater can drift away from the actor's evolving behavior. The post examines co-adaptation and failure modes such as over-deletion and empty procedures when appropriate training constraints are removed.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Different frameworks can substantially change the performance of identical models.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: DuMateBench reconstructs 200 real user workflows mixing coding, web research, document handling, and content creation. It evaluates the complete agent framework rather than assuming a model's capability transfers unchanged between scaffolds. With Claude Sonnet 4.8, the post reports scores ranging from 0.5821 to 0.8548 across compared frameworks.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: Harness-of-Harness supports software work across multiple days.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Harness-of-Harness wraps a coding agent in repeated planning, implementation, testing, and revision cycles that can continue over days. It aims to maintain direction while improving the product, rather than treating every execution as an isolated coding attempt. A case study reports more than 70 cycles producing a playable first-person shooter with gameplay, narrative, interfaces, graphics, and audio.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: Codebook Agent learns reusable collaboration structures for agent teams.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Codebook Agent studies reusable communication structures for multi-agent systems. It asks which topologies a learned generator must represent and whether convenient optimization proxies reflect actual execution costs. The post emphasizes checking the search space and representation before assuming a model can reliably rank or generate better collaboration graphs.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: VoiceMem targets fast memory retrieval for spoken interaction.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: VoiceMem targets memory retrieval fast enough for live spoken conversations, reporting a 134 ms retrieval window. The discussion argues that conversational memory involves multiple forms of context, including emotional context, rather than a single database search. The product question is whether this richer memory can improve interaction without creating perceptible conversational delays.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: LatentPress investigates compressing conversational context beyond ordinary text storage.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: LatentPress explores storing compressed context in a machine-oriented latent representation rather than a human-readable summary or an image that must be decoded back into text. The post treats natural language as an optional interface between memory and reasoning. It identifies adaptive decisions about what to preserve exactly and how much to compress as an important remaining challenge.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: E-Commerce Bench evaluates agent behavior across extended interactions.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: E-Commerce Bench runs agents through a simulated year managing several stores, evaluating 18 frontier models along seven dimensions. No model dominates every dimension. The post highlights differences between profit, operational behavior, and learning over repeated interactions, including an open model improving supplier negotiations across successive orders.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Autonomous research can produce convincing reports with unreliable experimental results.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A scientific-agent study checks whether manuscript claims match actual execution evidence. The post reports severe hallucinations in 90% of Agent Laboratory papers and 46% of Co-Scientist papers when reliability modules are removed. Restoring log-based checks reduces the cited rate to 4% and eliminates complete data fabrication in that experiment, showing why report quality alone is insufficient.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: A paper moves agent improvement into the execution of a task.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: PILOT adds a supervisor that watches a worker's trajectory, intervenes or aborts when needed, and writes useful procedures and failure modes into persistent memory. Improvement therefore happens during execution rather than only after a completed run. A correction can help the current attempt immediately and also become available to future workers.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Scientific model development becomes search over recorded executable experiments.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: AgentFold searches protein-folding model designs through executable code snapshots. Agents propose architectural changes, observe experimental outcomes, retain both successes and failures, and use tree search to allocate further compute. Starting from a compact ESMFold-derived system, the post reports an advantage over independent Codex proposals, emphasizing accumulated experimental evidence rather than isolated suggestions.

posts.author: David Sauerwein
posts.summary: Netflix treats model judges as systems requiring their own evaluation lifecycle.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A Netflix engineering account treats model judges as production components with a lifecycle, not metrics validated once and then trusted indefinitely. Human reference data, ongoing evaluation, and maintenance are needed as generated content and workloads change. The post warns against using an uncalibrated model to certify another model's work when human evidence is scarce.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Harness choices affect coding performance when context space is constrained.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A controlled Yuj comparison holds the model fixed while changing context reduction, stall detection, and command safeguards. The treatment shortens older tool outputs but preserves the complete record elsewhere. The post emphasizes that the intervention is a bundle rather than an isolated mechanism, and that benchmarking should describe the full solver: model, tools, memory policy, and execution controls.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: A paper categorizes failure mechanisms in self-evolving agent systems.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: HarnessEvolve addresses three problems in evolving agents: terminal rewards obscure which action caused failure, updates memorize narrow task patterns, and new changes erase prior capability. It separates task execution from diagnosis, revision, and update gates. The post reports results across open and enterprise settings, arguing for explicit safeguards rather than uncontrolled scaffold rewriting.

posts.author: Steven Dillmann
posts.summary: Terminal-Bench-Science reports adoption in a frontier model evaluation.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Terminal-Bench-Science reports its use in an Anthropic release evaluation shortly after launch. The post cites an increase from 24.7% for Claude Fable 5 to 52.6% for Fable 5.1 and links both the benchmark and release. It is an early adoption and model-comparison update, not a claim that scientific workflows are solved.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: An outer harness supports autonomous coding over several days.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Harness-of-Harness organizes an existing coding system into repeated, verifiable development increments, balancing repairs against new functionality. It preserves continuity over extended projects rather than requiring a new base agent. Across three benchmark families and three harness-model pairs, the post reports a 52.25% average relative gain after three iterations, with a higher peak improvement.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A study explores extending agent capability through harness design.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: openJiuwen allows the execution scaffold to adapt during a run while keeping the model policy fixed. Progress and feedback reshape context handling and task control instead of leaving capabilities permanently wired at initialization. The post reports 82.6% on SWE-bench Verified and 87.19% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, attributing those gains to the surrounding runtime.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: A driving system brings perception, planning, and language processing together.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Qwen-Driver retains a pretrained vision-language architecture while combining 3D perception, visual question answering, and motion planning. The post contrasts its shared representation with independently trained perception and planning modules. Its main architectural question is whether jointly represented driving capabilities can reduce the coordination overhead of a conventional modular stack.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A controlled comparison tests graph memory against flat retrieval.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A controlled memory comparison represents conversation turns as typed graph nodes and edges, then retrieves two-hop subgraphs under a fixed candidate budget. On LongMemEval, the graph's reported token F1 is 0.42 versus 0.47 for flat retrieval. A separate pruning pass removes roughly 10% of stored graph content without reducing F1, suggesting maintenance benefits need not imply better retrieval accuracy.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Google investigates reliability and efficiency in extended agent tasks.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: SKILL.state replaces an ever-growing execution conversation with an explicit state abstraction for extended agent tasks. The motivation is that retaining every observation, action, and reasoning trace increases processing cost and can pollute future decisions. The post reports improved accuracy with lower cumulative token usage across multiple settings and describes the abstraction as portable across skill runtimes.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Cache eviction choices may affect how language models should be trained.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Learning how to Forget matches fine-tuning behavior to the KV-cache policy used during deployment. If sparse attention evicts context at inference, training with a different memory regime can create failures. The post also describes making gradient computation practical for arbitrary cache policies, including a 4B-model example on a 40 GB A100.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Executable feedback offers an alternative source of learning beyond text corpora.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The discussion argues that spatial generation needs executable feedback analogous to compilers and tests in coding. Image-text similarity scores can miss whether a 3D scene satisfies actual constraints. Game engines are presented as a way to generate more checkable feedback for post-training spatial world models rather than relying only on larger visual datasets.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: A weekly research roundup highlights agent skills, evaluation, and scientific applications.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The August 24–30 reading list covers Skill Lift, JIT-Agent, Prime Agent, judge lifecycles, scientific research in real laboratories, instruction loss under compaction, and context management as code. It connects recent papers on agent learning, verification, memory, and practical scientific workflows.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Distilled models may inherit reasoning patterns associated with their teachers.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A distillation study argues that students transfer reasoning patterns associated with a teacher's lineage, not simply the teacher's factual knowledge or headline benchmark score. The post reports that a weaker related teacher can outperform a stronger unrelated one and that even simple mathematics can supply much of the benefit. It challenges choosing a teacher by capability rankings alone.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: A survey connects separate human-understanding tasks through foundation models.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A human-centric AI survey connects pose estimation, avatars, motion, interaction, generation, and control into a broader foundation-model agenda. It argues that individually strong components remain fragmented. Shared representations, appropriate data, physical grounding, and joint evaluation are presented as prerequisites for demonstrating that these abilities work together.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Memory-aware inference software enables larger models on limited laptop hardware.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: FreeToken adapts expert placement and execution to the actual memory and transfer characteristics of a local machine. Some computation is sent to the GPU while other experts run from system memory, with allocation based on measured bandwidth. The post reports a 35B model at 39.3 tokens per second on an 8 GB gaming laptop, emphasizing software-hardware coordination.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: An alternative improvement scheme separates a fixed improver from its targets.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Metan freezes an improvement operator and adds layers that can inspect the code and traces produced below them. It deepens the process only while performance improves. Each layer can revise or roll back earlier strategies using accumulated evidence, while leaving the mechanism responsible for improvement unchanged to reduce the risk of corrupting it.

posts.author: Samuel Schmidgall
posts.summary: Gemini is tested in practical scientific discovery workflows.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Google studies Gemini-assisted discovery at different autonomy levels in materials science, biology, and computer science, alongside a controlled study of AI-generated research papers. The settings range from human-executed synthesis to fully autonomous computational work. The announcement emphasizes practical research workflows and evidence validation rather than a single abstract science benchmark.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Memory and recall failures limit reliability on extended agent tasks.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A long-horizon benchmark asks an agent to operate a football club for 20 simulated years, using 26 tools and roughly 340–400 decision points. Scoring comes from a deterministic engine rather than a model judge. The post highlights persistent failures in learning hidden market prices and maintaining useful memory, which often becomes either an expanding archive or repeatedly rewritten plans.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Netflix combines generation, automated judging, and human audits for recommendation explanations.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Netflix describes an operational loop in which a model writes recommendation explanations, a judge scores them, and humans conduct recurring audits. The associated paper treats judges as components requiring calibration and ongoing maintenance as workloads change. Reported user behavior shifts include more discovery of unfamiliar titles and more browsing sessions ending in playback.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: A benchmark examines disagreement between model judges and expert assessments.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A dialogue-evaluation benchmark uses complete professional human-written conversations and more than 36,000 turn-level annotations to compare automated judgments with expert assessments. The post reports weaknesses in reference-free judging. A Mixture-of-Judges approach combines several evaluative signals and improves correlation with human ratings by roughly 30% in the cited comparison.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Stanford studies more efficient use of extended reasoning at inference time.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A Stanford study reduces the attention memory required for extended reasoning while keeping the total memory budget bounded. The post reports approximately threefold acceleration without additional training while matching full-attention performance. The approach also enables RL rollouts beyond 100,000 tokens, targeting the memory burden of the very tasks that require the longest reasoning.

posts.author: Shubham Saboo
posts.summary: A persistent wiki helps agents organize accumulated experience.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A persistent wiki retains not just revised agent skills but the reasoning and experience behind those revisions. The proposer can consult this accumulated history rather than rediscover old failures after each optimization round. The post reports a 15-point average performance increase when that wiki is available to the agent proposing new skills.

posts.author: Vlad Savinov
posts.summary: An interactive teaching tool visualizes distributed model training.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: An interactive website visualizes distributed training concepts such as fully sharded data parallelism, expert parallelism, and context parallelism. Users can manipulate compute elements to develop intuition about training traces. The project complements written scaling guides with a visual tool rather than introducing a new distributed training algorithm.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Microsoft investigates how supervised training supports subsequent reinforcement learning.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Microsoft asks whether conventional supervised fine-tuning creates the best starting distribution for subsequent RL. Repeated updates on already-fitted sequences can reduce the diversity that RL needs to explore. The post reports higher-coverage checkpoints improving final GRPO pass@1 by up to 3.9 points and accelerating early reward growth in some comparisons.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: An enterprise architecture discussion examines reusable agent runtime primitives.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A PwC paper argues for standardizing enterprise agents around a common loop, memory, filesystem, and shell interface rather than building bespoke frameworks for every use case. Its stated benefit is simplifying review and governance: differences move into inspectable instructions instead of separate codebases. The argument is organizational as much as a claim about runtime performance.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A prompt optimizer explores budget savings using a single evolutionary lineage.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: NPO keeps a single prompt lineage instead of managing a large candidate population or search tree. Each iteration uses student execution traces to guide another revision. The post reports matching GEPA with fewer rollouts and finds larger advantages as the teacher becomes stronger, suggesting improved proposer judgment may reduce the need for elaborate optimizer-side search.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Anthropic studies using one model to improve another model's alignment.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: An Anthropic research loop uses Claude agents to propose alignment changes, train a model, inspect hidden-evaluation feedback, and iterate. The post highlights a setting where the model receiving corrections is stronger than the one performing parts of the improvement work. Humans still define the rules and evaluation boundaries, limiting what the autonomous loop is authorized to optimize.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Explicit execution state may replace ever-growing agent conversation histories.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: SKILL.state supplies explicit current execution state instead of repeatedly appending and rereading the full transcript. The post reports lower token use and often better accuracy, including a cited comparison with a 16.2× token difference. Its boundary is important: the design works only if the state schema can represent everything the agent will need later.

posts.author: Sara Hooker
posts.summary: A research team shares an update on its new workspace.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Sara Hooker shares a workplace update from Adaption, celebrating furnishing a new office after starting with a largely empty room. This is a team and company milestone rather than a research result.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: PILOT studies improvement during extended agent execution.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: PILOT keeps model weights fixed while a supervisory runtime monitors progress, repairs the current trajectory, and records useful experience for later work. The distinction is between changing behavior through the harness and retraining the model. Its proposed benefit is recovering an ongoing run while retaining the lesson instead of paying to rediscover the same failure repeatedly.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: VoiceMem supports rapid retrieval for conversational speech models.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: This VoiceMem post emphasizes memory access within a reported 134 ms retrieval window for real-time speech. It argues that conversational systems need more than fact lookup, including context that supports coherent and emotionally appropriate interaction. The goal is to retrieve that information without introducing a noticeable additional pause.

posts.author: Shubham Saboo
posts.summary: An open agent repeatedly modifies and tests its own implementation.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: An open agent forks its own code, tests proposed changes, merges successful versions, and discards failed branches. The announcement reports more than 50 commits to its own implementation and describes a small Bash-based harness. It illustrates a concrete self-editing development loop, although the short post does not establish generalization or independent safety guarantees.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: A survey argues that scaffold selection deserves systematic evaluation.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A survey of terminal agents combines literature synthesis with matched-task diagnostics. The post reports measurable differences between scaffolds where changing the model variant within one scaffold adds latency without resolving more tasks. Its conclusion is that the execution framework should be treated as a first-order experimental and engineering choice.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: A study examines what research autonomy adds beyond constrained workflows.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A study of open-world mathematical discovery examines whether agents gain useful capabilities when allowed to choose their own research directions. The post reports proofs and generalizations not explicitly requested by an evaluator. It also notes that theorem-guided pruning helps some search spaces more than irregular construction problems, limiting broad claims that autonomy alone improves every task.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Evaluating a skill document does not establish its practical runtime benefit.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A skill-evaluation study compares the same task with and without a skill and examines whether the agent actually discovers and follows it. Structural and model-judge scores show essentially no correlation with measured capability lift in the cited results. The post argues for paired execution and trajectory analysis rather than certifying a skill from its document quality.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Shared skill libraries create new risks for cooperating coding agents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: EvoMal plants a malicious skill as an authoring template; agents can copy its payload into new skills and later execute those descendants. Removing the original therefore does not necessarily remove the attack. The post reports persistence over repeated rounds and a counter-prompt that reduces propagation substantially, highlighting provenance and reuse as part of skill-library security.

posts.author: Steven Dillmann
posts.summary: Terminal-Bench-Science introduces evaluation tasks grounded in scientific workflows.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 introduces 70 research-workflow tasks built with scientific domain experts, Stanford, the Laude Institute, and the Terminal-Bench team. The benchmark is intended to evaluate agents on practical scientific work rather than isolated academic questions. The release invites broader community participation and continued task development.

posts.author: Shafiq Joty
posts.summary: A self-distillation paper examines whether likelihood signals provide useful token credit.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Privileged Likelihood is not Automatically Value questions the token-level supervision used in on-policy self-distillation. Reference solutions, critiques, or other privileged information may change a token's likelihood without identifying its causal contribution to success. The paper proposes validating the credit signal before optimizing it rather than assuming likelihood changes are automatically useful rewards.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Apodex separates persistent task state from the model's immediate context.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Apodex 1.1 moves persistent task state outside the immediate message history and treats executable environments as part of the scaling strategy. The post emphasizes real interactions with files, commands, artifacts, and coordinated work rather than adding a larger tool catalog alone. It frames reliable execution as learning to operate within a richer workspace.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Dynamically generated harnesses offer an alternative to manually maintained scaffolding.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: JIT-Agent generates an agent harness for a task rather than using one permanently hand-written runtime. The report positions scaffold construction itself as model output. The post cites gains for multiple base models, including DeepSearchQA and OdysseyBench comparisons, and says the generated harnesses can compete with established coding-agent runtimes.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Researchers infer automata from recorded agent behavior.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Researchers induce compact finite-state machines from agent execution traces across 12 public datasets. The reported machines contain seven to 43 states and replay held-out data with 0.997 fitness. The post connects behavioral structure to the deployment harness and describes predicting failure from partial runs early enough to support stopping before completion.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: DarwinX improves web-agent scaffolding while keeping model weights fixed.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: DarwinX evolves prompts, tools, and control flow while keeping model weights fixed, addressing the risk that a single revised agent helps one task but harms another. The post reports web-task success rising from 43.5% to 93.0% and discusses testing transfer across tasks, verifiers, and base models. The gains are attributed to scaffold evolution rather than model fine-tuning.

posts.author: Avi Chawla
posts.summary: A coding workflow assigns planning, implementation, testing, and review to separate agents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: The post discusses a role-based coding experiment with planner, implementer, tester, and reviewer agents, where coordination reportedly consumed more tokens than the substantive work. It uses handoff information loss to question dividing work only by job title. The accompanying repository promotion should be distinguished from the experimental lesson about communication overhead.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Prime Agent uses a memory hierarchy to support extended reasoning.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Prime Agent combines model context with a persistent IPython session and disk-backed histories, prompts, and skills. The agent moves information between memory levels using code rather than relying only on lossy compaction. The post reports an ARC-AGI-3 result of 95.5% for Opus 5 and frames long inputs as searchable, transformable data.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Explicit research procedures may matter more than naming a preferred method.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: ASI-Bench holds research goals, data, and scoring fixed across 60 projects in 11 fields while varying how much procedural guidance the agent receives. Merely naming a method can constrain the direction while leaving implementation details unresolved. The post argues that explicit steps carry more useful information than method names and can avoid unnecessary reconstruction work.

posts.author: Robert Nishihara
posts.summary: A report discusses using alternative models to lower research inference costs.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Robert Nishihara reports from a talk that Periodic Labs uses Kimi to reduce inference costs by 20–50× compared with frontier APIs. The short post provides no controlled cost analysis or workload breakdown, so it is best treated as a practitioner observation and pointer to the talk.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A paper examines managing reusable skills for extended agent work.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Recuris separates task-progress working memory from reusable experiential memory, targeting failures that grow with task length. The post reports gains for GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5, including Opus reaching 87.9%. Benefits widen on the longest tasks, with some common failure types reduced by up to 80%, emphasizing memory organization rather than weight changes.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Escalating tasks between agents introduces coordination and context transfer costs.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: AWS measures the consequences of switching models partway through a coding run. Escalating from a weaker agent to a stronger model incurs a handoff cost; switching downward can occupy a better cost-quality point. The post also finds that retaining the earlier trajectory has different effects in the two directions, so model routing should account for inherited context.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: A memory evolution method adapts experiential and working memory in agent harnesses.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Recuris evolves working memory for unresolved task state and experiential memory for reusable lessons, without retraining the underlying model. The discussion treats failed runs as opportunities for small, testable repairs rather than undifferentiated context growth. Its design goal is preserving both current progress and the evidence needed to improve later executions.

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Google explores improving training environments instead of only changing agents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: EnvHarness adapts an existing training environment to the agent rather than replacing the agent or relying on a permanently fixed task collection. The wrapper changes what the agent encounters as its capabilities evolve. The post reports improved outcomes with 9.8% fewer execution steps in a cited comparison, arguing that training worlds must keep pace with the learner.

posts.author: Shivani Poddar
posts.summary: A founder shares early experiences building Wajo AI.

external_links.title: Announcing Fo: Wajo's first action agent Announcing Fo: Wajo's first action agent youtube.com

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A Wajo AI founder describes using agents to coordinate scheduling, communication, and other work during a difficult personal period. The story is presented as an early sign that one request can lead to useful action across several workflows. It is a personal product experience rather than a controlled capability evaluation.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: ClawGym II trains agents through realistic, opaque deployment harnesses.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: ClawGym II applies RL through unchanged deployment systems such as Claude Code and OpenClaw. Sandboxes run the harness, while model calls are intercepted at the serving boundary, allowing training without access to internal orchestration logic. The post reports gains extending to JobBench and OfficeQA, connecting training more closely to the framework used at deployment.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Microsoft distinguishes occasional task success from repeatable operational reliability.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Thinkingbox tests repeated execution in stateful business workflows and checks database outcomes rather than trusting an agent's final reply. The best reported system succeeds at least once on 91% of tasks but every time on only 25%. Many failed runs still end politely after a database-write tool call, demonstrating why isolated success and convincing completion messages are insufficient reliability measures.

posts.author: Dr. Ashish Bamania
posts.summary: DeepMind studies recirculation as an inference-time architecture technique.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Recirculation feeds information from deeper transformer layers back into earlier layers at inference, supporting an evolving internal state without changing weights. The post reports results on Gemma 3 and little additional generation latency, while noting serial processing during prefill. It examines recurrent computation as an architectural inference mechanism rather than a conventional fine-tuning update.

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Coding agents may remove visible symptoms without fixing underlying defects.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: SWE-bench Science tests real scientific software defects and distinguishes eliminating a visible failure from restoring the intended scientific computation. The post reports that agents can anchor on supplied explanations instead of checking them against executable evidence. Domain knowledge alone therefore does not reliably close the gap between passing visible tests and fixing the underlying defect.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Harness differences complicate comparisons between agent leaderboard results.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A harness-comparison study examines how context construction, tools, validation, retries, and stopping rules influence leaderboard scores. The post reports substantial score swings for the same models across scaffolds. It proposes a seven-layer Harness Card so comparisons can disclose whether a result reflects the base model, the runtime, or their interaction.

posts.author: Meni Brief
posts.summary: A developer describes using one coding assistant to coordinate another.
posts.details: Meni Brief describes a development workflow that uses one assistant to plan and supervise Codex implementation agents, with separate review and repair stages. The post also discusses terminal-level controls for spawning and observing a fleet. It is a personal orchestration recipe, not a controlled comparison establishing the superiority of a particular model combination.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Context compaction may weaken retained safety rules and coding instructions.

external_links.title: Claude Code overview - Claude Code Docs

posts.details: A study of 20 production agent configurations finds that ordinary compaction treats persistent rules and episodic history similarly, even though rules need stronger retention. A type-aware design assigns different retention policies and deterministic operators to compaction, partitioning, and retrieval. The post reports preserving two to four times more safety instructions and 96% recall over five rounds.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Richer environments help a mid-sized model tackle professional tasks.
posts.details: Apodex 1.1 combines richer executable environments with agent coordination to improve professional task performance using a 35B model. The post frames the workspace as an important capability surface alongside the model. Training on environment and coordination traces is intended to convert realistic, messy execution into behavior that can be repeated reliably.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: Prime Agent focuses on the runtime and memory constraints around models.
posts.details: Prime Agent supports extended work through persistent runtime state and a memory hierarchy rather than only a model's active context. The discussion warns that retaining skills also preserves bad discoveries, including exploits. It therefore pairs persistence with restricted permissions, independent verification, provenance, and rollback instead of assuming memory automatically produces safe improvement.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A survey clarifies terminal-agent definitions and conflicting harness comparisons.
posts.details: This post recommends a survey of terminal agents that clarifies the category and examines why reported harness comparisons conflict. It serves as a reading pointer for understanding command-line agent systems, with no additional experimental details in the captured text.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Growing skill libraries need consolidation and effective reuse.
posts.details: ContinualSkillBench asks whether growing a library of self-generated skills actually improves future capability. The post reports that carrying forward context and feedback accounts for much of the benefit, while reliable abstraction into reusable procedures remains difficult. Its implication is that consolidating and using skills may matter more than increasing the number of generated documents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: AgentMercury generates business scenarios with verifiable outcomes.
posts.details: AgentMercury synthesizes executable business scenarios with verifiable outcomes, expanding the worlds available for training. The post reports fine-tuning increasing held-out environment-authoring success from 3.3% to 83.3%. It also argues that interacting with diverse stateful scenarios can teach transferable planning, state tracking, constraint satisfaction, and precise tool use.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Scientific software tasks expose limitations beyond ordinary code engineering.
posts.details: SWE-bench Science comprises 119 real tasks from 98 repositories across 20 scientific domains. The post reports that the strongest coding agent remains below 50%, with failures reflecting scientific understanding as well as software engineering. It emphasizes evaluating whether a change preserves what the code is supposed to compute, not only whether the patch looks plausible.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Netflix describes maintaining useful automated judges in production.
posts.details: Netflix describes maintaining judges for hundreds of thousands of recommendation explanations each week, treating evaluation as a multi-phase lifecycle rather than one-time certification. A six-week experiment involving tens of millions of members reportedly improves discovery and browse-to-play outcomes against a no-explanation comparison. The account connects calibration and continuing oversight with a deployed product setting.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Stuart Winter-Tear
posts.summary: A discussion examines how tools, memory, and rules shape agent operation.
posts.details: A commentary on EnvHarness asks whether the environment around an agent deserves the same deliberate design as the agent runtime. The wrapper can change starting conditions, observations, and interaction possibilities. The post extends this idea to organizations, where human and automated capabilities need operating structures that turn them into coordinated action.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Code review systems face tradeoffs in agent team size.
posts.details: Adversarial Review explores explicit, structured disagreement among three code-review agents instead of simply expanding a cooperative team. The post reports diminishing returns from adding agents and stronger F1 when disagreement is deliberately elicited. It also notes that useful conflict must be limited, organized, and grounded in repository evidence rather than disagreement for its own sake.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: James Zou
posts.summary: Physics of Agents investigates collective behavior in interacting AI systems.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Physics of Agents studies more than 10,000 communities of interacting language-model agents and asks whether their collective behavior follows compact predictive laws. The post connects opinion dynamics with statistical physics. Its goal is understanding emergence, coordination, and alignment at the population level rather than inferring group behavior from isolated-agent benchmarks.

posts.author: Dawn Song
posts.summary: Vero tests repository-scale software construction with formal verification.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Vero evaluates whether agents can construct software repositories whose implementations satisfy machine-checked specifications. It targets guarantees that ordinary testing and review cannot provide across all possible inputs. The announcement says current agents are not yet reliably capable of repository-scale verified development and releases the benchmark, curation pipeline, and evaluation harness.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Task model induction aims to improve computer-use workflows.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Task Model Induction converts screen recordings and mouse or keyboard events into symbolic descriptions of how work is performed. It aims to recover reusable, auditable procedures from messy human demonstrations. The post reports a 30% improvement in held-out task accuracy over its strongest workflow-induction comparison, connecting passive interaction traces to computer-use agent skills.

posts.author: Chen-Yu Lee
posts.summary: Environment harnesses adapt the worlds used to train and evaluate agents.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: EnvHarness wraps a fixed environment with programmable controls over starting states, observations, available actions, and chains of episodes. This applies scaffold engineering to the world an agent learns in rather than only to the model's runtime. The announcement presents environment adaptation as a way to expose weaknesses and support further capability growth without replacing the environment itself.

posts.author: Federico Bianchi
posts.summary: TTT-Discover explores learning during scientific search at test time.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: TTT-Discover uses reinforcement learning during problem solving instead of keeping the model permanently frozen at test time. The announcement points to discovery results across mathematics, GPU kernels, algorithms, and biology. It advertises a research presentation and Q&A and links both the paper and event registration.

posts.author: Kshitiz Khandelwal
posts.summary: An inference engineering discussion examines per-token latency.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: An inference explanation connects token-generation latency to memory bandwidth and weight reads. Speculative decoding can reuse an expensive target-model pass to verify multiple draft tokens, but its value depends on how often those tokens are accepted. The post emphasizes draft-target compatibility and acceptance rate rather than assuming speculation automatically accelerates every workload.

posts.author: Jiachen (Amber) Liu
posts.summary: A Caltech event hosts a discussion of accelerated scientific research.

external_links.title: Science x AI Summit 2026 (Caltech) · SAIR Science x AI Summit 2026 (Caltech) · SAIR sair.foundation

posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Jiachen Liu announces a Caltech SAIR discussion on accelerating scientific work with AI. The brief post provides a talk announcement and acknowledgments rather than a research methodology or evaluation result.

posts.author: Shubham Saboo
posts.summary: Soup aims to make model fine-tuning practical on limited local hardware.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: Soup streams model layers so fine-tuning need not keep the complete base model on the GPU. The announcement reports an 8B-model example on a 4 GB laptop GPU and an Apache-2.0 release. It also highlights the author's willingness to retract an earlier explanation after measurement contradicted it, emphasizing empirical validation of the optimization story.

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: DeepMind studies the computation required to choose specialist models.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).
posts.details: A DeepMind routing paper includes the cost of estimating which specialist model is valuable, rather than treating that estimate as free. It relates the problem to optimal search with costly inspection. The post argues for value-of-information decisions that call expensive estimators selectively and notes that noisy estimates can introduce strategic distortions.

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Google develops environments that adapt as agents improve.
posts.details: Google's EnvHarness adds a programmable layer to static training environments, diagnoses weaknesses, creates changes targeting them, and validates the changes with fresh rollouts. Across five benchmarks in four domains, the post reports improvements of up to nine points on held-out instances with 9.8% fewer execution steps. The emphasis is adapting the learning environment as the agent changes.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: Google explores improving training environments instead of only changing agents.
posts.details: EnvHarness argues that fixed task collections can stop challenging a learner as its capabilities improve. A wrapper reshapes the environment without replacing the underlying implementation. The cited results include 9.8% fewer execution steps, emphasizing environment design as another optimization surface alongside model architecture and reward functions.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Winston Weinberg
posts.summary: Harvey introduces Tenet for specialized legal model applications.
posts.details: Harvey introduces Tenet, post-trained with Fireworks AI for extended legal workflows. The announcement connects open-weight models with firm-specific specialization and describes internal knowledge access through memory and structured notes. It links further training and benchmark details rather than presenting the model as a general substitute for legal professional judgment.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: Task-CoEvolve reduces harness optimization cost through validation task selection.
posts.details: Task-CoEvolve reduces the expense of harness optimization by adapting which validation tasks each candidate must face. Instead of spending the full budget on another scaffold proposal, it seeks a smaller evaluation that still distinguishes close candidates and unresolved capabilities. The post frames validation selection as a central part of efficient agent improvement.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Thai Duong
posts.summary: A security researcher discusses AI-driven changes in vulnerability research.
posts.details: Thai Duong reflects on how stronger AI tools are changing vulnerability research and the resources needed to participate effectively. The post emphasizes access to capable infrastructure and research teams and includes a hiring link. It is a practitioner and recruitment commentary rather than a detailed exploit methodology.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: DAIR.AI
posts.summary: Amazon considers the research corpus as part of an agent's infrastructure.
posts.details: CTIFoundry constructs structured knowledge and action surfaces at indexing time instead of leaving the corpus as opaque embedding chunks. With the agent harness otherwise unchanged, the post reports overall F1 gains of 0.19–0.28 across four models. A smaller model on the structured substrate reportedly beats a flagship on the flat corpus using roughly half as many tool calls.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Pratik Bhavsar
posts.summary: Continual harness learning aims to improve while retaining earlier behavior.
posts.details: Harness Continual Learning applies retention concerns to prompts, memory, skills, and routing, not just model weights. A rule that repairs one failure can break previously working tasks. The post recommends versioned candidate artifacts, replaying earlier tasks, keeping proposed changes separate from deployed state, and rolling back updates when historical behavior regresses.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A paper studies ongoing updates to prompts, skills, and agent memory.
posts.details: A continual harness-learning framework commits revisions only after checking new-task improvement, historical retention, and validity. It treats prompts, memory, tools, skills, and routing as persistent components that can forget or interfere with one another. The post reports relative gains above 10% across reasoning, multimodal perception, and open-world interaction.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Model interactions may expose proprietary skill instructions.
posts.details: A black-box skill-stealing study tests whether ordinary interaction can reveal proprietary agent skill files. Across five commercial models, the post reports even a basic extraction prompt recovering 48% exactly on average, with a high judged leakage ratio. It argues that embedded instructions remain extractable data, not automatically protected intellectual property merely because users cannot view the source file directly.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: A study investigates mechanisms behind the effectiveness of agent skills.
posts.details: A study of 8,135 trials argues that skills often help by stabilizing action sequences rather than injecting missing knowledge. It describes this as procedural anchoring: inconsistent execution becomes a clearer procedure. Failures arise when assumptions are brittle, context is incompatible, or the agent cannot adapt the procedure, making runtime fit more important than document polish alone.
