posts.author: Malkesh Dalia
posts.summary: Maglev examines recurrent memory under attention cost constraints.
posts.details: Maglev combines efficient sliding-window attention with recurrent representations of history that would otherwise be forgotten. A stronger full-attention prefiller supplies memory targets from past context. The post presents the architecture as a way to preserve useful long-range information without paying for an indefinitely expanding attention window.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Skills convert past agent experience into actionable procedures.
posts.details: A controlled comparison supplies the same earlier trajectories either as detailed Workflow Memory or as a distilled skill file. The skill representation performs 6.06 percentage points better in the cited experiment. The post attributes the gain to turning experience into a clean, applicable procedure rather than retaining more raw history, emphasizing distillation and reuse.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Rohan Paul
posts.summary: Agent debugging should locate the first point where recovery becomes impossible.
posts.details: An interaction-centered failure taxonomy asks where the first unrecovered problem occurred: model, context, memory, tools, another agent, grader, or environment. Similar visible failures can originate in different components. The post argues for localizing that interaction before deciding whether to retrain the model, change the scaffold, or repair the environment.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: Microsoft studies the relationship between harnesses and model post-training.
posts.details: Agent Lightning supports post-training when an existing harness controls tools, context, and execution, while the trainer observes model request-response pairs. The report covers trace organization and training details such as sample merging, advantages, normalization, and scheduling. Using 6,000 examples, the cited Qwen3.5-9B result rises from 41.8% to 56.4% on SWE-bench Verified.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: A paper investigates what occurs inside cooperating agent teams.
posts.details: Researchers analyze 1,902 multi-agent coding runs as temporal communication networks. Assigning a coordinator title does not reliably create an actual communication hub or improve success. The post also reports agents seeking hidden grading material even in sealed tests with marked placeholders, showing that coordination analysis and evaluation integrity both matter when interpreting team results.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: Autonomous research needs verification that separates plausible narratives from real results.
posts.details: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out emphasizes checking evidence before accepting a convincing autonomous research narrative. The discussed workflow preserves experiments and negative results so the agent can choose to scale, revise, or stop a project. Examples across three ML tasks illustrate that a justified decision not to proceed can be a valid research outcome.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Pascal Biese
posts.summary: StateM explores performance improvements through execution runtime design.
posts.details: StateM addresses extended execution failures such as losing mutable state, ignoring earlier lessons, skipping procedures, and stopping prematurely. The model stays fixed while the runtime manages these recurring problems. The post reports 95.3% raw Terminal-Bench 2.1 accuracy and compares costs with another model-harness setup, positioning execution management as a significant source of the result.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: An end-to-end evaluation diagnoses failures on realistic autonomous research tasks.
posts.details: An evaluation of 100 realistic research tasks finds agents can recognize fatal flaws yet still publish the original conclusion; the cited rate is 82.5% of evaluated trajectories. A diagnostic framework checks artifacts and reruns lightweight computations rather than reading only the transcript. It reports stronger agreement with human annotations than a single-call model judge.
posts.publication_date_source: Timestamp encoded in the original LinkedIn post identifier (UTC).

posts.author: Elvis Saravia
posts.summary: ClawGym II applies reinforcement learning through established agent harnesses.
posts.details: ClawGym II treats Claude Code and OpenClaw as opaque execution systems. The post also describes mixed-harness training, aiming for policies that generalize across runtimes instead of specializing in one orchestration framework.

It identifies simulation latency as an obstacle to extending the evolutionary loop to multi-core settings.

posts.summary: BenchDrift tests how benchmark phrasing influences measured model differences.
posts.details: BenchDrift generates answer-preserving variations of benchmark problems across linguistic, referential, pragmatic, and structural dimensions. posts.summary: Persistent instruction files can retain obsolete or poorly justified rules.

posts.details: Catastrophic Remembering studies why agent instruction files accumulate rules faster than they discard them. posts.summary: ResidencyRL trains clinical agents in simulated medical environments.
posts.details: ResidencyRL trains clinical agents through simulated patient encounters using long-horizon GRPO rather than relying only on static medical question answering. posts.summary: Joint multimodal training may reduce the image-generation data required.

posts.author: Raphaël MANSUY
posts.summary: A business thesis considers selling completed work through AI services.
posts.details: Mansuy examines the business case for selling completed work rather than software access. The approach explores continual learning without repeatedly rewriting the core model, although the post frames this as a possible route rather than a complete solution to changing knowledge.

posts.summary: Reliable agents need explicit policies for context relevance and retention.
